title: Relocation of the Aft Galley Waste Line Joint and Drain Mast Interface

ata.title: Waste Disposal — Waste Tank and Drain

abstract: Cancelled proposal to move the aft galley waste line joint away from the cabin floor penetration and to re-make the drain mast interface with a heated cartridge, after repeated seepage into the insulation blankets below the aft galley.

sections.reason: Cabin crew reports of dampness and odour at the aft galley, together with maintenance findings of saturated insulation blankets below the galley floor, pointed at the waste line joint that sits directly above the floor penetration. Seepage at that joint is not visible from the cabin and is only found when the galley is removed. Eleven aircraft were affected across four operators in three years. The proposal was to move the joint 600 mm outboard, away from the penetration, and to replace the drain mast interface with a heated cartridge that would stop the ice plug that occasionally backs the line up in the cruise.
sections.description: The waste tank latch assembly D3830122463596 was to be replaced by a version with the outlet rotated 90 degrees, and the right-hand waste tank panel D3830127394574 re-cut to suit. The inboard partition position 70WP was to be moved outboard with the joint, and the inboard panel position 73WP9 replaced by a drip tray with a witness drain routed to an existing overboard point. The forward galley insert position 37WP was to be re-secured to the new bracket. Protective sleeving AES710749-83 and spacers LN562957-2B were specified for the revised run, and the tubular spacer set was to be deleted from the cancelled portion. All work was inside the aft galley and the aft lavatory complex, zones 941, 943, 945 and 983, with the galley monument removed. Detail was carried on drawings D38300046331 and D38300057532.
sections.effects: The proposal carried a mass increase of 7.2 kg per aircraft and an electrical load increase of 220 VA for the heated cartridge. It was cancelled in 2020 after a cheaper answer was found: the joint sealing compound was changed under a supplier process change and the galley removal interval was aligned with the cabin refresh cycle, which together closed out the reported cases without a design change. No aircraft were modified, no service bulletin was issued, and no manual content was changed. The proposal is retained in the dossier because the underlying moisture path below the aft galley remains a live topic for the ageing fleet.
sections.embodiment_note: Cancelled before launch. No production cut-in was proposed and no retrofit vehicle was created.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft of the reference datum; CG shift below 0.02 % MAC
